audiopus_sys 0.2.2
License: ISC
Repository: https://github.com/lakelezz/audiopus_sys.git

Packaged source: vendor\audiopus_sys

# Relay patch to audiopus_sys 0.2.2

Upstream: https://github.com/lakelezz/audiopus_sys/tree/v0.2.2
Source: the crates.io audiopus_sys 0.2.2 archive, including its ISC license and bundled Opus source/license.

The only behavior change adds the explicit `livekit-opus` Cargo feature. Relay enables it only for Windows builds with `native-rtc`, where the pinned LiveKit `webrtc.lib` already exports the standard Opus C API used by the unchanged `opus` Rust wrapper. In that configuration, this binding crate supplies declarations without compiling or linking a second Opus implementation. Missing SDK symbols remain normal link errors. Other configurations use the original upstream build and bundled Opus.

This avoids duplicate native symbols in the optimized Windows build; it does not suppress linker errors, rename symbols, or modify the codec ABI. Upstream generated bindings and codec source are unchanged. See workspace/client manifests for feature wiring.

serenity 0.12.5
License: ISC
Repository: https://github.com/serenity-rs/serenity.git

Packaged source: vendor\serenity-0.12.5

# Relay TLS dependency patch

Source: https://crates.io/crates/serenity/0.12.5 (ISC; LICENSE.md retained).
Official crate SHA-256: `9bde37f42765dfdc34e2a039e0c84afbf79a3101c1941763b0beb816c2f17541`.

Cargo.toml and Cargo.toml.orig change: tokio-tungstenite 0.21.0 ->
0.24.0, with the explicit `url` feature that preserves the upstream URL API.
This moves the Discord gateway from rustls 0.22/webpki 0.102 to
the shared, patched rustls 0.23/webpki 0.103 stack without changing the
Serenity API or its Rust implementation. Runtime implementation, build script and license retain upstream behavior/terms.
The token-validator documentation example now uses an obvious noncredential
placeholder accepted by the same three-part format check, replacing an upstream
Discord-token-shaped literal rejected by GitHub push protection. No token is
validated against Discord, and no runtime validation logic is changed. Unused packaged Cargo.lock and CI
metadata are omitted. Replace this patch when upstream ships a compatible
release using a supported TLS stack.

The retired stack matches RUSTSEC-2026-0049, 0098, 0099, 0104, 0346,
0349 and 0382 (some IDs alias GHSA records); version matches alone do not
establish exploitability in Relay's fixed Discord endpoint.

webrtc-sys-build 0.3.19

# Relay native exception bridge correction

Based on the exact locked `webrtc-sys-build` 0.3.19 crate. Original files and hashes are recorded in `upstream-source.json`; source copyright is LiveKit 2025, Apache-2.0, with the terms reproduced in `LICENSE`.

The original correction excludes `_HAS_EXCEPTIONS` when importing prebuilt SDK defines. The official SDK's `webrtc.ninja` sets `_HAS_EXCEPTIONS=0`. Its C++ wrapper nevertheless throws `std::runtime_error` and uses CXX try/catch to return errors to Rust, while CXX is built with normal C++ exception support. Mixing these MSVC exception representations produced an invalid error-string pointer at `cxxbridge1$exception` during removal from a closed peer connection.

The change applies to the wrapper's compilation only. The pinned SDK archive, its headers/library, media transport, encryption, codec and other imported ABI defines are unchanged. Compiler exception support and ordinary error propagation are preserved; Rust's undefined-behavior checks are not disabled.

Verification uses `actual_native_closed_peer_returns_error_without_abort`: an unnegotiated video sender, closed peer, and 32 error returns without network, physical capture or account data. It reproducibly aborted before the patch and returns all 32 valid errors after the patch. The final eight native opt-ins also pass, including terminal DuplicateIdentity cleanup, signal resume, full reconnect, Stop during recovery, generated application audio and synthetic hardware H264. See `docs/verification-rtc-recovery-0.10.0.json` for exact source/binary/log hashes and limitations. This verifies these local regressions, not all possible native failures or physical/WAN acceptance.

The subsequent native frame cryptor patch adds Cargo invalidation for `LK_CUSTOM_WEBRTC` and the selected `lib/webrtc.lib`. This prevents cached native link metadata from keeping an older library path when the SDK generation changes. It does not change wrapper ABI. The original archive remains intact; a separately prepared generation replaces its cryptor object, described in `docs/native-frame-crypto.md`. The earlier unchanged-library statement and regression record describe the original exception-only stage.
